info.title: Mayarin API
info.description: Create fiat-denominated commerce requests, accept supported crypto assets, and settle merchants in stablecoins. Versioned operations live under `/v1`; buyer-facing checkout, invoice, and health routes are intentionally unversioned.

post.description: Creates an immutable fiat-denominated payment request. Reusing an idempotency key with the same body returns the original intent; the same key with different parameters is a 409. The response also carries `payerToken` and `checkoutUrl`: the hosted payment page with the payer's token attached. Send that URL to the payer; the payment id alone opens nothing.

post.summary: Retry a failed payment whose funds arrived
post.description: Reopens a `FAILED` payment at `ASSET_RECEIVED` and replays the clearing steps, for a failure since fixed (a missing swap pool, an asset not yet whitelisted) while the payer's money sat at the deposit address. Every step is idempotent per state, so nothing that already happened happens twice. A deposit-match order whose deadline passed is re-signed with the same terms and a fresh deadline. Refused with 409 when the payment has not failed or its funds never arrived.

get.summary: What is for sale, across every merchant
get.description:
The cross-merchant discovery index: every resource a merchant has opted into the public index, newest first. Pass `merchant` instead to read one merchant's resources — the per-merchant read is not paginated and is not limited to listed ones.

Nothing is listed by default. Listing only decides whether a discovery reader is shown a resource; an unlisted resource is still payable by anyone holding its URL, because the URL is the access control.

get.description:
Invoices with an outstanding balance and fixed-amount payment links, across every merchant, newest first — what an agent reads before it has met anyone. Each entry carries the price a `402` would actually quote, so a reader deciding whether to pay need not ask each one.

Draft, void and paid-in-full invoices, disabled and expired links, and open-amount links never appear and never quote, listed or not.

get.summary: Quote one invoice or link — or settle it
get.description:
One endpoint, two answers, decided by the `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header. Without one: a `402` whose `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header quotes the **full** outstanding amount — an authorization for less than what is owed is refused, and the remedy is a new `402` for the whole balance. With one: verify, settle, and answer `200` naming the payment intent the settlement created.

A payable's price is held in a quote row for a short window together with the exact rails it offered, which is what the `409` and `410` are about.

400.description: Unknown payable kind, or a signature the chain did not accept.

402.description: Payment required. The price and rails ride the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header, base64-encoded.

404.description: No such payable, or it is not payable over x402.

409.description: Another authorization claimed this obligation first, or the amount signed is no longer the amount owed.

410.description: Quote expired — request a new `402` at the same URL.

get.summary: Which rail to pay on, and why
get.description: Returns the first accepted rail in merchant configuration. Every accepted rail has already passed capability and pricing checks; a payer may still choose another entry from the `402`.

404.description: No resource with that id, or x402 is not enabled on this deployment.

get.summary: Quote a resource without calling it
get.description: The price and rails, without making the call being decided about. Not part of the x402 specification — the price normally rides a `402` — but a client deciding whether to pay should not have to make the call first.

200.description: The price and the rails that offer it.

404.description: No resource with that id, or x402 is not enabled on this deployment.

post.description: Checks the signature against the chain without broadcasting. The body's `paymentRequirements` is not what gets verified — Mayarin rebuilds the requirements from the resource and uses the carried copy only to identify which quoted option the payer chose. A facilitator that verified against the requirements handed to it would verify a payment against its own claims.

200.description: The verdict — `isValid`, and the closed-set reason when false.

404.description: No resource with that id, or x402 is not enabled on this deployment.

post.summary: Broadcast it, and credit the merchant
post.description: The one that moves money: verifies authoritatively, broadcasts the transfer, confirms it on-chain, and posts the double-entry records that credit the merchant. The payment's nonce is the idempotency key server-side, so a second settle of the same authorization is refused rather than charged twice. An authorization that was valid but did not settle answers `200` with `success: false` and the reason in `errorReason`.

400.description: Validation error, or a signature the chain did not accept.

409.description: Quote conflict — the price or rails changed under the authorization.

410.description: Quote expired — request a new `402` at the same URL.
